title: Grothendieck category of sheaf dg modules
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space with a sheaf of commutative rings $\mathcal O$, in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal A$ be a sheaf dg $\mathcal O$-algebra, and use left sheaf dg modules and degree-zero chain maps as in [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization]. The category of these modules is Grothendieck abelian [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. Its kernels, cokernels, coproducts and filtered colimits are computed on underlying graded $\mathcal O$-module sheaves, with the induced differential and action. The forgetful functor to complexes of $\mathcal O$-module sheaves is exact and faithful. Filtered colimits commute with every underlying cohomology sheaf $H^n$.

source.place: Tags 0FRJ (lemma-dgm-abelian) and 0FS9 (lemma-dgm-grothendieck-abelian), with the degreewise kernel, cokernel and colimit constructions in section-dgm-abelian; left modules by the graded opposite algebra.

proof.text: Work on the small open site of $X$ in the prescribed universes. The cited sheaf-module statement gives kernels sectionwise and cokernels by module sheafification. For a dg map $f:M\to N$, $d$ and the action preserve $\ker f$ and $\operatorname{im}f$ since $f(dm)=df(m)$ and $f(am)=af(m)$. Thus they restrict to the kernel and descend to the presheaf cokernel; the cited bilinear-extension statement extends the quotient action to its sheafification. The identities $d^2=0$, associativity, the unit and Leibniz rule descend because they hold before taking the quotient. The kernel and cokernel universal maps respect both structures, so they have the dg universal properties. Hom groups, zero and finite biproducts are inherited componentwise. The underlying degreewise coimage-to-image map is an isomorphism in the abelian category of module sheaves; its inverse respects action and differential by composing their commuting squares with that inverse. This proves abelianness. The forgetful functor to complexes is faithful because a dg map is precisely an underlying chain map with a property, and exact because kernels and cokernels have just been computed degreewise.

For any small family $(M_t)$ take in degree $q$ the module-sheaf coproduct $\bigoplus_t M_t^q$, which exists by the cited ringed-site theorem. Concretely it is the sheafification of the presheaf of finite sums: its universal property follows from the sheafification adjunction. Define $d((m_t)_t)=(dm_t)_t$ and $a(m_t)_t=(am_t)_t$ on these sums; the cited bilinear-extension theorem extends the action to sheaves. The dg identities and the coproduct universal property follow on each summand, then on the sheafification by uniqueness. For a small diagram $F:I\to\mathrm{dgMod}(\mathcal A)$ put
$$C=\operatorname{coker}\!\left(\bigoplus_{\alpha:i\to j}F(i)\longrightarrow\bigoplus_iF(i)\right),$$
where the component indexed by $\alpha$ is $\iota_jF(\alpha)-\iota_i$. A map out of this cokernel is exactly a family $h_i$ satisfying $h_jF(\alpha)=h_i$, so $C$ is the colimit. The identical cokernel formula in module sheaves proves that its underlying graded sheaf is the degreewise colimit. This covers coproducts, filtered colimits, and the empty colimit.

source.place: Tags 0FR0 and 0FRJ, direct sums and colimits; explicit cokernel presentation of the colimit.

proof.text:
Exactness in dg modules is now exactness in every degree of module sheaves. Apply exact filtered colimits in the cited ringed-site theorem to every degree of a diagram of short exact sequences. The degreewise-colimit construction in step 2 proves exactness of filtered colimits of dg modules. For a filtered diagram of underlying complexes $K_i$, write $Z_i^q=\ker d_i^q$ and $B_i^q=\operatorname{im}d_i^{q-1}$. Apply the same exact colimit functor to
$$0\to Z_i^q\to K_i^q\to B_i^{q+1}\to0,\qquad 0\to B_i^q\to Z_i^q\to H^q(K_i)\to0.$$
The inclusions $B_i^{q+1}\hookrightarrow K_i^{q+1}$ remain monic, so the first sequence identifies the colimit of the $Z_i^q$ with the kernel of the colimit differential and the colimit of the $B_i^{q+1}$ with its image. The second sequence then identifies $\varinjlim_iH^q(K_i)$ with $H^q(\varinjlim_iK_i)$. These identifications use the original cocone maps, hence give the canonical comparison. No boundedness is used.

source.place: Tags 0FR0 and 0FRJ, exact filtered colimit paragraphs and the following definition of underlying cohomology.

proof.text:
For an open $U$ and $n\in\mathbf Z$ define $E_{U,n}$ over $\mathcal A_U$ as the graded free left module on $e,f$ of degrees $n,n+1$, with $de=f$, $df=0$. Explicitly,
$$d(ae)=d(a)e+(-1)^{|a|}af,\qquad d(af)=d(a)f.$$
The two contributions to $d^2(ae)$ are $(-1)^{|a|+1}d(a)f$ and $(-1)^{|a|}d(a)f$, so they cancel; $d^2(af)=0$. The algebra Leibniz identity gives the module Leibniz identity on both free generators. A dg map $E_{U,n}\to M|_U$ must send $e$ to some $m\in M^n(U)$ and $f$ to $dm$; conversely the assignments $ae\mapsto am$, $af\mapsto a\,dm$ define such a map, since $d(am)=d(a)m+(-1)^{|a|}a\,dm$. Therefore these dg maps are naturally in bijection with $M^n(U)$. This is the explicit two-generator disk calculation underlying the cone-of-identity argument; it avoids any shift-sign ambiguity for left modules.

source.place: Tag 0FS8 (remark-cone-identity), local disk calculation used in the proof of Tag 0FS9.

proof.text:
Use the cited open-extension adjunction with $L=E_{U,n}$. The preceding bijection becomes
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{dg}\,\mathcal A}(j_{U!}E_{U,n},M)\simeq M^n(U).$$
The indexing pairs $(U,n)$ form a set in the chosen universe. Form $G=\bigoplus_{U,n}j_{U!}E_{U,n}$ by step 2. If $h:M\to N$ is nonzero, then some $h^n(U)$ is nonzero on a section $m$. The corresponding map $j_{U!}E_{U,n}\to M$ has nonzero composite with $h$. Extend it to a map $G\to M$ by taking zero on all other summands. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}(G,h)$ is nonzero, so $\operatorname{Hom}(G,-)$ is faithful and $G$ is a generator. Together with abelianness, all small colimits and exact filtered colimits already proved, this is exactly the cited definition of Grothendieck abelian. Steps 1--3 give all the additional clauses of the item.
